sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: irender-ui-kit is a set of components in the style of shadcn/ui for iRender documents. Each one is plain configuration: a type, props, and the usual attrs, style, parts and on. The kit sets defaults only, so a document can override any attribute, style or inner part. Colours, radius, spacing and fonts come from theme tokens, so the whole kit follows a theme, dark mode included.

sections.title: Theming
sections.summary: The kit reads its colours, radius, density, text size and font from theme tokens. Theme options let people choose between sets of them on the page, and the choice is kept and applied before the page shows, on every page that uses the kit. The light and dark mode is a theme option too.

sections.title: Button
sections.summary: A button in seven variants and four sizes, with an optional icon. With href it renders a link that looks like a button. Its on.click runs any actions.

sections.title: Split button
sections.summary: A primary action joined to an arrow that opens a menu of related ones, such as Download PDF with Excel and CSV in the menu.

sections.title: Toggle, toggle group and slider
sections.summary: A toggle is a button that stays pressed. A toggle group presses one option (or several with multiple). A slider picks a number in a range. All three keep their value in state through bind.

sections.title: Form controls
sections.summary: Inputs, text areas, selects, checkboxes, switches and radio groups, styled to match. bind keeps a state key in sync both ways; name makes them work in a plain form.

sections.title: Field, input group and button group
sections.summary: A field lays out a label, a control, help text and an error, and wires them together for screen readers. An input group puts text or buttons inside a field's border. A button group joins buttons into one control.

sections.title: Combobox
sections.summary: A searchable select in the style of react-select: one or many values, groups, options loaded as you type, creatable values, fixed values, and the WAI-ARIA combobox keyboard.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-combobox
  props:
    bind: flavours
    multiple: true
    clearable: true
    options: [{ value: vanilla, label: Vanilla }, { label: Fruity, options: [mango, lime] }]
- { type: ui-combobox, props: { bind: city, searchUrl: /api/cities, placeholder: Search cities… } }

sections.title: One-time code
sections.summary: A code in a row of boxes, for two-step sign-in or confirming an email. Typing, pasting and the phone's suggestion of a code from a message all work, as one field for the keyboard and screen readers. The pattern keeps out what doesn't belong, and a complete event fires when the last box fills.

sections.title: Number input
sections.summary: A number or an amount, grouped in the locale's way as it's typed (1,25,000 in India, 125.000 in Germany) while the caret stays among the same digits. State gets a plain number. A currency puts its symbol first; Up and Down step it, as do optional − and + buttons; leaving the field clamps it to min and max.

sections.title: JSON editor
sections.summary: A JSON text area for payloads and advanced settings: highlighted, with line numbers, checked as you type with the line and a plain reason for any error, and Format. The value reaches state only while the text is valid.

sections.title: Date picker and calendar
sections.summary: Pick a day (with a time), a month, a quarter or a year; one, a range or several. Limits, disabled days, presets, financial years and typing the date are props. bindRange gives the exact dates picked, ready for a chart's or a table's filter, and compare adds a period to compare them with: the one before, last year's, or one picked.

sections.title: Colour picker
sections.summary: Pick a colour on a saturation and brightness area with hue and opacity sliders, type any CSS colour, take one from the screen with the eyedropper, or choose from swatches. It's written to state as hex, rgb or hsl, ready for a style or a chart; custom: false makes it a palette of set colours.

sections.title: File upload
sections.summary: Files from a drop zone, uploaded with their progress, shown as a grid or a list, previewed (images, PDFs, CSV and Excel sheets, text) and downloaded together as a zip. The files are kept in state, so a form can send them; type, size and count limits are checked as they're added.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-file-upload
  props:
    bind: receipts          # [{ id, name, size, url, status, progress }]
    url: /api/upload        # multipart, field `file`; answer { id, url }
    accept: "image/*,.pdf,.xlsx"
    maxSize: 10 MB
    hint: Images, PDFs or spreadsheets, up to 10 MB

sections.title: Rating and password checklist
sections.summary: ui-rating picks a rating with stars (a click or the arrow keys, hover to preview, click again to clear), or shows one read-only, filling part of a star for an average. ui-password-checklist goes under a password input and ticks its rules as they're met, with a strength bar; bindValid tells a button when the password is good enough.

sections.title: Form
sections.summary: A form that checks its fields by rules as they're left and when it's submitted, runs its submit actions only when all is right, and knows its unsaved changes: a bar saves or discards them, and leaving asks first. Fields go in columns, and sections group them under a heading with columns of their own; the two mix.

sections.title: Stepper
sections.summary: The steps of a process and the current one's panel, with Back, Next and Finish. A step can be gone to once the ones before it are done, or say they're valid. Across or down the page, without a script.

sections.title: Repeater
sections.summary: Rows of fields to add, fill in, reorder, copy and remove, kept as a list of objects in state. Computed fields and totals follow, and each field can be checked.

sections.title: Sortable list
sections.summary: A list in state put in order: drag an item's grip with a mouse, a finger or a pen, or from the keyboard (Space picks it up, the arrows move it, Space puts it down, Escape puts it back). Items can be removed, numbered, and drawn with your own content; the new order goes straight back to state.

sections.title: Form builder
sections.summary: A form put together in the browser: field types from a palette (clicked or dragged), put in order by dragging or the keyboard, and set up in an inspector (label, key, help, choices, limits, required). Preview tries the form with its checks; Document gives it out as an iRender document of the kit's own form, ui-form with its rules, also kept in state.

sections.title: Import
sections.summary: Rows from a spreadsheet: a CSV or Excel file (or pasted cells) is read in the browser, its columns matched to the fields by name, its rows put right in an editable table, and the good ones handed over or posted in batches.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-import
  props:
    bind: draft
    bindImported: contacts
    url: /api/contacts/import
    fields:
      - { field: name, label: Name, required: true, aliases: [contact] }
      - { field: email, label: Email, required: true, unique: true }

sections.title: Tags, masks, phone and time
sections.summary: Inputs with a shape of their own: tags typed one after another, text in a fixed shape, a phone number with its country, a time typed any way or picked, and text that names people with @.

sections.title: Tree select and transfer list
sections.summary: Choosing from a hierarchy, in a field that opens a searchable tree; and choosing from a long list, moved from one list to another and put in order.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-tree-select, props: { bind: department, nodes: "{{ departments }}", path: true } }
- { type: ui-transfer-list, props: { bind: columns, options: "{{ allColumns }}", reorderable: true } }

sections.title: Query builder
sections.summary: Conditions put together with and / or, nested in groups and negated, for segments, alerts, routing and access. State gets the query, the query in words, and the rows that match.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-query-builder
  props:
    bind: query
    rows: "{{ orders }}"
    bindMatches: matching
    showText: true
    fields:
      - { field: total, label: Total, type: currency, currency: EUR }
      - { field: status, label: Status, type: select, options: [Paid, Due] }

sections.title: Signature and image cropper
sections.summary: A signature drawn with a finger, pen or mouse, or typed; and a picture cropped, turned and zoomed. State gets each as a picture.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-signature, props: { bind: signed, bindMeta: signedBy } }
- { type: ui-image-cropper, props: { bind: photo, ratio: ["1", "16 / 9", free] } }

sections.title: QR code, barcode and scanner
sections.summary: QR codes and barcodes drawn in the page as SVG, without a service, to show, save or print; a QR code takes a logo (a picture, an icon or letters); and a scanner that reads them with the camera where the browser can, or from a field.

sections.title: Code editor
sections.summary: Code or a template typed over its highlighted copy: line numbers, indenting, closing brackets, comments with ⌘/, words offered as it's typed, and problems marked on their lines.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-code-editor
  props: { bind: query, language: sql, completions: [select, from], diagnostics: "{{ problems }}" }

sections.title: Badge, status badge and kbd
sections.summary: A badge is a small status label: solid, outlined, or a soft wash of `info`, `success`, `warning` or `destructive`, with an optional `dot` for a status. kbd shows a key or shortcut. ui-status-badge shows a status in its colour: Done, Paid and Approved green, In review and Pending amber, Blocked and Overdue red, and so on, with tones for your own.

sections.title: Card
sections.summary: A bordered panel with an optional icon, title and description. Put a card footer last for its actions. `variant` picks `elevated`, `outline` or `muted`, and `href` makes the whole card a link that lifts when hovered.

sections.title: Avatar and aspect ratio
sections.summary: An avatar shows a picture, or initials when there's none. An aspect ratio keeps its children at a fixed shape as the width changes.

sections.title: Table
sections.summary: A styled HTML table in a scrolling container. Its children are the table's rows and sections, so a list with tag: tbody fills it from data or state. For sorting, filters and paging, use the data table.

sections.title: Data table
sections.summary: A table over rows with sorting, column filters, search, paging or infinite scroll, rows from an API, virtual rows, nested rows, pinned columns, selection with bulk actions, detail rows and summaries. Its filters are the chart kit's, so tables and charts filter each other.

sections.title: Filters
sections.summary: Filters for a list in a side panel: lists to pick from, numbers and amounts, dates and text, each with its operators (is any of, between, before, contains, is empty, …). The applied filters show as chips; Apply writes them to state as { field: condition }, the same object a data table's or chart's filter takes, or an API. Date filters have presets (Last 7 days, This month, This quarter, …), and bindViews keeps named views of the filters to come back to.

sections.title: Tree
sections.summary: A hierarchy to browse, select, check, search, add to, delete from and rearrange: drag a node onto another, or move it with Alt and the arrow keys. It follows the ARIA tree pattern for the keyboard and screen readers. With bindNodes the tree edits its own nodes in state; every change also fires an event for a host to save.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-tree
  props:
    nodes: "{{ places }}"        # { id, label, children }
    bindNodes: places           # moves, adds and deletions are written back
    bind: picked                # the selected id; bindNode: the node itself
    checkable: true
    bindChecked: checked
    addable: true
    deletable: true
    movable: true
    search: true
    counts: true

sections.title: Kanban board
sections.summary: Columns of cards to drag between, or to move with Alt and the arrow keys: the new order goes back to state, with a move event for a host to save. Cards show tags, a priority, a due date and who has them; columns can have a limit and fold away, and Add card asks for a title.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-kanban
  props:
    columns: [ { id: todo, title: To do }, { id: doing, title: Doing, limit: 3 }, { id: done, title: Done } ]
    cards: "{{ tasks }}"   # [{ id, column, title, tags, assignee, priority, due }]
    bindCards: tasks
    addable: true

sections.title: Event calendar
sections.summary: Events in a month grid, a week of hours, or a list by day, coloured by category. Overlapping meetings sit side by side in the week; events over several days run across them. A click on an event or a day goes to state, for a details panel or adding one; the arrow keys move through the days.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-event-calendar
  props:
    events: "{{ events }}"   # [{ id, title, start, end, category }]
    categories: { Meetings: info, Maintenance: warning }
    bindEvent: event
    bindDay: day

sections.title: Activity timeline
sections.summary: Who did what and when: an avatar or initials, the action and time, field changes as old → new, and comments. Events without a person get a dot in a tone. Entries come from children or from state, and redraw as it changes.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-timeline
  props: { items: "{{ history }}" }   # [{ who, action, when, changes, comment, tone }]
  children:
    - { type: ui-timeline-item, props: { who: Asha Rao, action: changed the status, when: 2 h ago, changes: [ { field: Status, from: Open, to: Done } ] } }

sections.title: Code block
sections.summary: Code, highlighted, with line numbers, marked lines and a copy button. The code can come from state: an object shows as JSON.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-code-block
  props: { language: yaml, title: hello.yaml, lineNumbers: true, highlight: ["3-4"], code: "..." }

sections.title: Typography and separator
sections.summary: Headings in four levels, text in variants from lead to code and blockquote, and a separator line, plain or with a label in the middle.

sections.title: Editable table
sections.summary: A data table whose columns have edit works like a spreadsheet: the arrow keys move between cells, typing edits, Tab goes on, Shift picks a range to copy, paste (from a spreadsheet too), fill down or clear, and undo takes edits back. required, min, max, pattern and unique mark cells that are wrong, and a button shows only their rows. Edits go to the state the rows come from.

sections.title: Stat
sections.summary: A figure with its change from before, a small trend line, and progress to a target. A change's colour says whether it's good.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-stat
  props: { label: Revenue, value: "{{ revenue }}", format: currency, currency: EUR, previous: 41000, changeLabel: vs last month, trend: [3, 5, 4, 6, 8] }

sections.title: Gauge
sections.summary: A figure on a dial from min to max: coloured bands for good, warning and bad (the value takes its band's colour), a target mark and a needle, as an arc or a semicircle. Drawn on the server, it follows state without a script; for screen readers it's a meter read with its band's name.

sections.title: Description list and items
sections.summary: Labels and their values, copied or edited in place; and things in a list, each with an icon, image or initials, a title, a description and actions.

sections.title: Comments
sections.summary: Comments in threads: replies, mentions, reactions, resolving, and editing one's own. Each change is written to state and fires an event.
sections.usage: - { type: ui-comments, props: { bind: thread, user: "{{ me }}", people: "{{ people }}", resolvable: true } }

sections.title: Lightbox
sections.summary: Pictures as a grid, a row, a masonry or a stack, that open over the page to zoom, move and step through. Without a script, each is a link to its picture.
sections.usage: - { type: ui-lightbox, props: { images: [ { src: a.jpg, caption: One }, { src: b.jpg } ], max: 6, download: true } }

sections.title: Pivot table
sections.summary: Rows summed up by fields down and across, with subtotals that fold, shares of a total, a heat tint, sorting by any column, an export, and the rows behind a cell.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-pivot
  props:
    rows: "{{ sales }}"
    down: [region, rep]
    across: [date]
    values: [ { field: amount, agg: sum, format: currency } ]
    fields: [ { field: date, label: Quarter, part: quarter } ]
    editable: true
    bindCell: cell

sections.title: Scheduler
sections.summary: Bookings against time, a row per person, room, vehicle or machine: moved, stretched and made by dragging or the keys, with working hours, capacity, and clashes marked or not let happen.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-scheduler
  props: { resources: "{{ rooms }}", events: "{{ bookings }}", bindEvents: bookings, bindEvent: picked, from: "08:00", to: "18:00", creatable: true }

sections.title: Plan
sections.summary: Things placed on a drawing: rooms, seats, bays, beds, plots, machines. It zooms and moves, picks one or several, colours by status and filters, and moves what's dragged. Aircraft cabins, buses, trains, cinemas, theatres, auditoriums, stadiums, halls, car parks and offices come from a few words, and a building can have several floors with stairs and lifts between them.

sections.title: PDF
sections.summary: A PDF on the page: zoomed, its text selected, and marked with highlights, boxes, notes and signatures kept in state. pdf.js is loaded only when there's one to show.
sections.usage: - { type: ui-pdf, props: { src: /files/contract.pdf, bindNotes: notes, tools: [highlight, note, signature], signature: "{{ signed }}", height: 640 } }

sections.title: Diff
sections.summary: Two versions compared: text or code line by line, side by side or unified, with the words that changed; or two records field by field.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-diff, props: { before: "{{ old }}", after: "{{ new }}", language: yaml } }
- { type: ui-diff, props: { mode: fields, before: "{{ was }}", after: "{{ now }}", fieldLabels: { name: Name } } }

sections.title: Log
sections.summary: Lines that follow as they arrive: levels to filter by, a search that marks matches, wrapping, terminal colours, and saving to a file.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-live-data, props: { url: /api/log, into: lines } }
- { type: ui-log, props: { lines: "{{ lines }}", title: Deploy, height: 320, download: deploy.log } }

sections.title: Alert
sections.summary: A callout for a short, important message, with an icon, a title and a description. `info`, `success`, `warning` and `destructive` each bring their colour and icon; children such as buttons go under the description, and `dismissible` adds a ✕.
sections.usage: - { type: ui-alert, props: { variant: warning, title: Your trial ends soon, description: Add a payment method to keep your projects., dismissible: true } }

sections.title: Toast
sections.summary: A message that shows for a few seconds at the bottom of the screen. Put one toaster on the page, bound to a state key; setting that key to a title and description shows a toast. `variant` (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `destructive`) gives it a colour and an icon, and a bar counts down its time.

sections.title: Notifications
sections.summary: A bell with an unread count that opens a panel: Unread and All, a dot to mark one read or unread, archive, and Mark all as read. Notifications come from state and changes go back to it; a click opens one, marks it read, and closes the panel. inline puts the panel in a page.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-notifications
  props:
    items: "{{ notifications }}"   # [{ id, title, body, who, when, read, tone }]
    bindItems: notifications
    bindItem: opened
    allHref: /notifications

sections.title: Illustrations, error pages and empty states
sections.summary: Drawings for error pages and empty states: not found, server error, forbidden, maintenance, offline, no data, no results, out of stock, an empty cart or inbox, no notifications, an expired session, a failed payment, coming soon and all done. They're coloured by the theme's primary colour and its second brand colour, with neutrals mixed from the text and background, so they follow the palette, custom colours and dark mode. Give ui-empty an illustration for an empty state; the blocks have whole error pages.

sections.title: Progress, progress ring and skeleton
sections.summary: A progress bar for a task's completion, and skeletons that stand in for content while it loads. ui-progress-ring is the same as a ring, with the value in the middle.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-progress, props: { value: "{{ progress }}" } }
- { type: ui-skeleton, props: { width: 240, height: 16 } }

sections.title: Spinner, empty state and scroll area
sections.summary: A spinner says something is loading. An empty state fills a page or list with nothing in it yet. A scroll area scrolls its children with a thin, themed scrollbar.

sections.title: Banner
sections.summary: A message across the page: maintenance, an offer, a trial's end, a setting to finish. It can be closed and stay closed, keep to an edge, come and go at set times, and count down.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-banner
  props: { title: Maintenance, text: "Saturday 22:00 to 23:00.", tone: warning, bind: closed, remember: maint-12, countdown: "2026-12-05T22:00" }

sections.title: Tour and session timeout
sections.summary: A tour points at parts of the page one after another, for someone new to it. A session timeout asks whether someone's still there before their session ends, across their tabs.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-tour
  props:
    bind: tour
    id: welcome
    autoStart: true
    steps:
      - { target: "#search", title: Find anything, text: Press / to start. }
- { type: ui-session-timeout, props: { after: 20, warn: 2, extendUrl: /api/session, signOutUrl: /login } }

sections.title: Dialog, alert dialog, sheet and drawer
sections.summary: A modal dialog opened by its trigger; an alert dialog that only its own buttons close; a sheet that slides in from an edge; and a drawer that slides up from the bottom and closes with a drag down. A dialog close button closes the one it's in, and runs its own actions too.

sections.title: Popover, dropdown menu, tooltip and hover card
sections.summary: Floating content next to its trigger: a popover for anything, a dropdown menu of actions with the menu keyboard, a tooltip on hover or focus, and a hover card for a preview.

sections.title: Context menu
sections.summary: A menu opened with a right-click (or Shift+F10, or the menu key) on its area, at the pointer. bind gets what was right-clicked: the nearest data-context value, or a data table's row.

sections.title: Command palette
sections.summary: A search box over a list of actions, filtered as you type, inline or in a dialog opened with a shortcut such as ⌘K.

sections.title: Tabs, accordion and collapsible
sections.summary: Tabs switch between panels, with the open one in state. An accordion opens one section at a time (or several with multiple), and a collapsible shows and hides one, both on native details.

sections.title: Menubar and submenus
sections.summary: A bar of menus, as at the top of an application. Left and Right move along the bar, and an open menu follows; Down opens a menu; hovering moves between open menus. Any menu can hold submenus, checkbox items and radio items.

sections.title: Navigation menu
sections.summary: A site's navigation: links, and items that open a panel of links (or anything else) on hover or click. Down opens a panel and moves into it, Escape closes it, and Left and Right move along the bar.

sections.title: Breadcrumb and pagination
sections.summary: A breadcrumb shows where a page sits, the last item being the current page. Pagination links pages, with the page and page count from data or state.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-breadcrumb, props: { items: [{ label: Home, href: / }, { label: Settings }] } }
- { type: ui-pagination, props: { page: "{{ page }}", pages: 12, href: "?page={{ p }}" } }

sections.title: Sidebar
sections.summary: A whole-page layout with a sidebar that collapses to icons or slides away, opens as a sheet on a phone, and toggles with ⌘B. Items can hold sub-menus, icons and badges.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-sidebar-layout
  props: { bind: sidebar, collapsible: icon }
  children:
    - type: ui-sidebar
      children:
        - type: ui-sidebar-content
          children:
            - type: ui-sidebar-group
              props: { label: Platform }
              children: [ { type: ui-sidebar-item, props: { label: Dashboard, icon: grid, href: /, active: true } } ]
    - { type: ui-sidebar-trigger }

sections.title: Rail layout
sections.summary: An app shell with a rail of icons down the left, each opening its own panel beside it, and the page's main content after: the layout of chat, mail and project apps. The section shown and whether its panel is open are state; a click on the open section folds its panel.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-rail-layout
  props:
    bind: section
    bindOpen: panelOpen
    items: [ { id: inbox, label: Inbox, icon: core:bell, badge: 4 }, { id: settings, label: Settings, icon: core:settings, bottom: true } ]
  children:
    - { type: ui-rail-panel, props: { for: inbox }, children: [ ... ] }
    - { type: element, children: [ ... ] }   # the main content

sections.title: Resizable
sections.summary: Panels side by side or stacked, with a line between each two that resizes them by dragging or with the arrow keys. Sizes are percentages, kept in state with bind; a collapsible panel folds away and comes back.

sections.title: Dashboard grid
sections.summary: Tiles on a grid of columns and rows, to drag by their header and resize from their corner, or move with the arrow keys on a focused header (Shift with them resizes). The tiles in the way move down, and the rest float up. The layout is kept in state with bind, a locked tile stays put, and on a narrow screen the tiles stack in one column.

sections.title: Scroll spy
sections.summary: Navigation that follows the reading: the in-page link for the section in view is marked (aria-current="location") as the page scrolls, and kept in view in a list that scrolls on its own. The sidebar of this page is one; use it for a table of contents beside a long article.

sections.title: Chat
sections.summary: A conversation log, message bubbles with threads and UI in them, a typing indicator, and an input that sends to an endpoint and streams the reply in.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-conversation, props: { messages: "{{ chat }}", typing: "{{ waiting }}" } }
- { type: ui-chat-input, props: { messages: chat, waiting: waiting, endpoint: /api/chat } }

sections.title: Attachments, sources and actions
sections.summary: What an assistant's messages show beside their text: files sent with them, the sources behind an answer with its [1]s as links, and what was done, or needs approving. A message's attachments and sources fields draw the first two.

sections.title: Trace and questionnaire
sections.summary: The steps of a run, nested and against time, each opening to what went in and out; and questions answered one at a time or together, for an assistant, a survey or an intake form.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-trace, props: { spans: "{{ run.spans }}", bindSpan: step } }
- { type: ui-questionnaire, props: { bind: answers, bindDone: done, questions: [ { id: pace, question: How full should the days be?, options: [Easy, Full], required: true } ] } }

sections.title: Carousel
sections.summary: Slides in a row that scroll sideways and snap to each one, with arrow buttons, keys and swiping. Chat replies use it for a set of cards.

sections.title: Install and update
sections.summary: The document's app settings (name, icons, colours, shortcuts, what's kept offline) make its pages an installable app: irender app writes the manifest, the icons and the service worker. These two offer to install it, with the browser's own prompt or the steps for an iPhone, and to reload once a new version has been fetched.

sections.title: Offline
sections.summary: Whether there's a connection, as a badge, a banner or a dot and in state; what was sent without one (submits, forms and uploads), kept and sent later, even after the app has been closed; and state kept on the device between visits.

sections.title: App shell
sections.summary: An app's frame: a bar with the screen's title and a Back button, the screen, and tabs at the foot, or down the side with room for them. It keeps clear of a phone's notch, remembers where each screen was scrolled to, can be pulled down to refresh, and can follow the phone's back button.

sections.title: Notifications and badge
sections.summary: Offers notifications at a good moment, says why before the browser asks, subscribes to pushes by topic and sends the subscription to your server; the app's service worker shows them. The badge is a number on the installed app's icon, and in the tab's title. On an iPhone both need the app on the home screen.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-push-opt-in
  props:
    publicKey: "{{ vapidKey }}"
    saveUrl: /api/push
    when: "{{ ordered }}"
    text: Know when it's on its way.
    topics: [ { value: orders, label: Orders }, { value: news, label: News, on: false } ]
    remember: orders
- { type: ui-app-badge, props: { count: "{{ unread }}" } }

sections.title: Sharing
sections.summary: Sharing a link, text or files with the device's own sheet, or a list where there's none; taking what other apps share with this one once it's installed; and contacts from the phone's list, a contact card file, or typed.

sections.title: Passkeys and app lock
sections.summary: Signing in with a fingerprint, a face or the device's PIN, where the server makes the challenge and checks the answer; and a lock over the app after a while, or once it's been out of sight, opened with a passkey or a PIN. The lock keeps out someone who picks up the device; it doesn't encrypt anything.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-passkey, props: { optionsUrl: /auth/options, verifyUrl: /auth/verify, bind: session, autofill: true } }
- { type: ui-app-lock, props: { after: 5, hidden: 30, digits: 6, bindLocked: locked, signOutUrl: /signout } }

sections.title: Camera
sections.summary: Photos from the camera: front and back, light, zoom, composing lines, an outline to fill, a timer, retakes and several shots, made smaller and stamped with the time before they're kept. Where there's no camera to use, the device's own picker.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-camera, props: { bind: photos, multiple: true, max: 6, stamp: "{{ site }} · time", grid: true } }
- { type: ui-camera, props: { bind: card, guide: card, ratio: "1.586" } }

sections.title: Photo mark-up
sections.summary: Arrows, boxes, circles, freehand, text and measurements on a photo, and blurring for faces and number plates. Give one measurement its length and the others are worked out. The marks are kept apart from the picture, and drawn onto a copy of it.
sections.usage: - { type: ui-photo-annotate, props: { src: "{{ photo }}", bind: marked, bindMarks: marks, unit: cm } }

sections.title: Permissions
sections.summary: One screen for what an app may use: why, whether it's allowed, a button to ask, and how to allow what was blocked, in this browser's own steps.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-permission-manager
  props:
    bind: allowed
    bindReady: ready
    permissions: [ { name: camera, reason: For photos of the work, required: true }, { name: geolocation, reason: To show where it was }, notifications ]

sections.title: Location and check-in
sections.summary: Where the device is, once or as it moves, with how accurate that is; and checking in and out of places, with the distance, the time, how long it's been and a photo. A device can be made to lie about where it is, so a check-in is a record, not proof.

sections.title: Field map
sections.summary: A light map for apps, drawn by the kit without a library, to draw on: markers that group when they're close, areas, circles and lines, where the device is, and drawing on it. The tiles are OpenStreetMap's unless you name your own, as an app should. For Google Maps, popups of any components or a lot of data, use the map kit's ui-map.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-field-map
  props:
    markers: "{{ places }}"
    cluster: true
    areas: [ { id: zone, lat: 38.714, lng: -9.133, radius: 300 } ]
    position: "{{ here }}"
    bindSelected: place
    draw: [marker, line, polygon, circle]
    bindDrawn: shapes

sections.title: Route tracker
sections.summary: Records a path while the app is open and in front: distance, time and speed, with pause, and GPX to save. Draw it on a map, and keep it with ui-local-store.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-route-tracker, props: { bind: route, download: route.gpx } }
- { type: ui-field-map, props: { lines: [ { points: "{{ route.points }}" } ] } }

sections.title: Compass and level
sections.summary: Which way the device faces and the way to a place, and a spirit level, from the device's own sensors. Either can show a value from elsewhere instead, such as the wind's.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-compass, props: { from: "{{ here }}", target: { lat: 38.72, lng: -9.15 } } }
- { type: ui-level, props: { bind: tilt, tolerance: 0.3 } }

sections.title: Recorders
sections.summary: Voice notes with a moving waveform, short videos with a time limit, and pictures or videos of a screen. Each pauses, plays back, and is kept as an object with a data: address that a form or a queue can send.

sections.title: Speech
sections.summary: Speech to text, shown as it's heard, and text or a part of the page read out with the device's own voices, marking each sentence. Where the browser can't turn speech into text (Firefox), transcribeUrl takes a recording.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-voice-input, props: { bind: note, iconOnly: true, transcribeUrl: /api/transcribe } }
- { type: ui-read-aloud, props: { target: "#article", controls: true } }

sections.title: Document scanner
sections.summary: Scans papers with the camera or from a picture: finds the page's edges, straightens it, cleans up shadows, and makes a PDF of several pages. All of it happens on the device.
sections.usage: - { type: ui-document-scanner, props: { bind: pages, bindPdf: pdf, filter: bw, paper: a4 } }

sections.title: Swipe and screen
sections.summary: A row that's swiped sideways to show what can be done with it, with a button for a mouse and the keyboard; and keeping the screen on while it's needed.

sections.title: NFC
sections.summary: Reads NFC tags held to the phone, and writes text or an address to them. Only Chrome on Android can; anywhere else it says so.
sections.usage: - { type: ui-nfc, props: { bind: tag, bindList: tags, write: "https://example.com/item/{{ item.id }}" } }

sections.title: Bluetooth
sections.summary: Connects to a Bluetooth Low Energy device, reads its values and follows those that change, and sends to it. Chrome and Edge can, not iPhones.
sections.usage:
- type: ui-bluetooth
  props:
    bind: sensor
    read: [ { key: rate, label: Heart rate, unit: bpm, service: heart_rate, characteristic: heart_rate_measurement, as: heart-rate, notify: true } ]
    commands: [ { label: Reset, service: heart_rate, characteristic: heart_rate_control_point, value: 1, as: uint8 } ]

sections.title: Serial and USB
sections.summary: A serial port a line at a time (scales, meters, microcontrollers), read as text, numbers, JSON or CSV; and USB devices that no driver has taken, such as label printers. Chrome and Edge on a computer.
sections.usage:
- { type: ui-serial, props: { baud: 9600, parse: number, bind: weight, send: true, commands: [ { label: Zero, text: Z } ] } }
- { type: ui-usb, props: { filters: [ { vendorId: 0x0a5f } ], commands: [ { label: Print, value: "{{ label }}" } ] } }

sections.title: Files
sections.summary: Opens a file and saves back to it, where the browser can, or as a download. Installed, the app can be what files open with: the document's app.files says which.
sections.usage:
app: { name: Notes, files: [ { url: "./", accept: { text/markdown: [.md] } } ] }
root: { type: ui-file-handler, props: { bind: file, accept: { text/markdown: [.md] }, save: "{{ draft }}", bindDirty: dirty } }
